stemMd: Why is a water molecule bent rather than linear?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The oxygen atom has two bonding pairs and two lone pairs of valence electrons.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Hydrogen atoms have large metallic lattices.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Only nuclear forces determine the bond angle.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The oxygen atom has no valence electrons.

explanationMd: Four electron domains around oxygen favour an approximately tetrahedral arrangement. Two are lone pairs, so the positions of the two hydrogen atoms form a bent molecule.

distractorRationale.e: Oxygen has valence electrons that participate in bonding.
distractorRationale.d: Valence-electron interactions govern the molecular geometry here.
distractorRationale.c: Hydrogen in water is covalently bonded.
